screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a map of the Earth's tectonic plates, or a cross-section through one plate boundary. Layers of real data can be drawn on top of it: plate boundaries coloured by type, plate motion arrows, earthquake epicentres, volcanoes and hotspots, and shaded relief of the land surface and sea floor.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a view selector, a checkbox for each data layer, an earthquake depth filter, controls that run plate motion forwards and backwards through geological time, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Switch on a pair of layers and look for where they line up — earthquakes and volcanoes around the Pacific, or ridges and shallow earthquakes down the middle of the Atlantic.

viewDetails.globe: The Earth is showing as a globe, which can be turned to bring any part of it into view.
viewDetails.subduction: A cross-section through the Chile trench is showing, where the Nazca plate subducts beneath South America.
viewDetails.divergent: A cross-section through the Mid-Atlantic Ridge is showing, where North America and Africa spread apart.
viewDetails.transform: A cross-section through the San Andreas fault is showing, where the Pacific and North American plates slide past each other.

depthDetails.all: Earthquakes of all depths are shown.
depthDetails.shallow: Only shallow earthquakes, less than 70 kilometres deep, are shown.
depthDetails.intermediate: Only intermediate-depth earthquakes, 70 to 300 kilometres deep, are shown.
depthDetails.deep: Only deep earthquakes, more than 300 kilometres deep, are shown.

timeDetails.present: Plates are in their present-day positions.
timeDetails.past: Plates are shown as they were about {{value}} million years ago.
timeDetails.future: Plates are shown as they would be about {{value}} million years from now.

controls.viewSelectorHelp: Choose the global map or a cross-section through one kind of plate boundary.
controls.globeToggleHelp: Draw the global map on a globe that can be turned, instead of a flat rectangular map.
controls.globeHelp: Drag the globe to turn the Earth. With the globe focused, the left and right arrow keys move the view east and west, and the up and down arrow keys move it north and south.
controls.depthFilterHelp: Show earthquakes of every depth, or only one depth band.
controls.timeSliderHelp: Move plates back into the past or forward into the future, in millions of years.
